![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13990291/assets/0b56d6a20b6a3e01dafa9770eb328ebaab5c14f76d87026c160c9be0d8926e74.png)

Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

The line segment $\overset{―}{AB}$ is shown above. Which of the following is $\overset{―}{{A}^{′}{B}^{′}},$ the image of $\overset{―}{AB}$ under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the image of $\overset{―}{AB}$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the endpoints of $\overset{―}{AB}:$

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 6 \\ 7 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective endpoints of the image are ${A}^{′}(-3,7)$ and ${B}^{′}(6,2),$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13990291/assets/ba458ff966132a67202469208f1daaaa98339ce22071247ca06d0f400c2e7390.png)

$$

A line segment $\overset{―}{EF}$ has endpoints at $E(1,1)$ and $F(2,3).$ What are the coordinates of the corresponding endpoints $\overset{―}{{E}^{′}{F}^{′}}$, the image of $\overset{―}{EF}$ under the action of $T?$

questions.worked_solution:
To find the image of $\overset{―}{EF}$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the endpoints of $\overset{―}{EF}:$

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$

To find the image of $T$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $△ABC:$

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 3 \\ -2 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}]

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 3 \\ -2 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 2 \\ -3 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of $△{A}^{′}{B}^{′}{C}^{′}$ are $(2,-3),(-2,1),(2,3)$, as shown below.

Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

A triangle $PQR$ has vertices at $P(-2,2),\,Q(2,3),$ and $R(0,-2).$ What are the coordinates of the corresponding vertices of  $△{P}^{′}{Q}^{′}{R}^{′}$, the image of $△PQR$ under the action of $T?$

${P}^{′}($ 
{{field-1}}, 
{{field-2}}
$),\,$  $\,{Q}^{′}($ 
{{field-3}}, 
{{field-4}}
$),\,$ $\,{R}^{′}($ 
{{field-5}}, 
{{field-6}}
$)$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the image of $△PQR$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $PQR:$

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 18 & -8 \\ 2 & 8 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

A triangle $XYZ$ has vertices at $X(2,0),\,Y(-4,2),$ and $Z(4,0).$ What are the coordinates of the corresponding vertices of  $△{X}^{′}{Y}^{′}{Z}^{′}$, the image of $△XYZ$ under the action of $T?$

questions.worked_solution:
To find the image of $△XYZ$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $XYZ:$

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 4 \\ 0 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}]

Consider the linear transformation $\mathbf T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

The line segment $\overline{AB}$ is shown below. Find $\overline{A'B'},$ the image of $\overline{AB}$ under the action of $\mathbf T.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13990291/assets/2e22400d15abc81150d6d18de591549e81a46bd16ab9e95f10f86bae2125b490.png)
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To find the image of $\overline{AB}$ under the action of $\mathbf T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the endpoints of $\overline{AB}\mathbin{:}$

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $\mathbf T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective endpoints of the image are $A'(1,3)$ and $B'(1,-2),$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13990291/assets/472f8e712f7d695d5ab3593dafbcc0309feb1a6ac80e9e29c4893dc651d20cf7.png)

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

The triangle $\triangle ABC$ is shown below. Find $\triangle A'B'C',$ the image of $\triangle ABC$ under the action of $\mathbf T.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13990291/assets/4986bd2dab6b455c0d5e41909377c433d761bf7270364d3e2596e6db7f23981b.png)
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To find the image of $T$ under the action of $\mathbf T,$ we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $\triangle ABC\mathbin{:}$

$$
[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 2 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $\mathbf T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 2 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & 1 \\ -4 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of $\triangle A'B'C'$ are $(-3,-4), (0,0), (1,-2),$ as shown below.
